findings.note: Gutierrez is listed among the authors (the bill was filed by another senator; he was added 2025-01-29). As filed, the bill amends how identification is shown at the polls: one form of photo ID, or a listed non-photo ID with a signed reasonable-impediment declaration, or two listed forms including one with the voter's current address. It also changes the paperwork for the disability exemption. Referred to State Affairs 2025-02-03; no later action shown.

Gutierrez is listed among the authors. As filed, any qualified voter would be eligible to vote early by mail; the bill's text keeps a driver's-license, state-ID or last-four-of-Social-Security-number item on the mail-ballot application. Referred to State Affairs 2025-02-03; no later action shown.

Gutierrez is listed among the authors. As filed, county registrars would automatically register a resident who is issued a certificate of naturalization, and a newly naturalized citizen could present the certificate to the registrar as the citizenship statement. Referred to State Affairs 2025-02-03; no later action shown.

Gutierrez is listed among the authors (first called session of the 87th Legislature). The caption is 'requiring a voter to present proof of identification'. Its text sets the same poll ID options as the 2025 SB 144 (photo ID, or listed non-photo ID with a reasonable-impediment declaration, or two listed forms).
Gutierrez is listed among the authors (second called session of the 87th Legislature). Same caption as SB 45: 'requiring a voter to present proof of identification'.

Gutierrez is the lead author (as a state representative). The bill, captioned as relating to disclosure of personal information on a driver's license application or motor vehicle record, would limit the Secretary of State's access to driver's-license data used to check voters for citizenship. Referred to the Elections committee 2019-02-27.

findings.passage: “We need to ensure that no illegal votes are cast, but we must do it with precision and integrity instead of targeting based on race. Texas is better than this.”
findings.note: Quoted by the San Antonio Current (article dated 2019-02-08) on the Texas Secretary of State's 2019 check of voter rolls against driver's-license records for non-citizens, and his bill HB 1450. The same article quotes his press statement that relying on the driver's-license data fails to account for people who became naturalized citizens after applying for a license.
